==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|cephalick|q1=archaic}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰebʰ-}}
{{ety|en|:bor|frm:cephalique|tree=1}}
From {{uder|en|frm|cephalique//cephalicque}}, from {{der|en|la|cephalicus||cephalic}}, from {{der|en|grc|κεφαλικός||cephalic}}, from {{af|nocat=1|grc|κεφαλή<t:head>|-ικός<t:-ic>}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|sĭfăl' ĭk|a=US}}, {{IPA|en|/sɪˈfælɪk/}}; occasionally {{IPA|en|/ˈsɛfəlɪk/}} in parallel with [[cephalad|/ˈsɛfəlæd/]] and [[cephalo-|/ˈsɛfəl(oʊ)-/]].
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-cephalic.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Of or relating to the [[head]].
## Of or relating to the [[brain]].
##* {{RQ:Swift Gulliver|part=III|page=78|passage=I was at the Mathematical School, where the Maſter taught his Pupils after a Method ſcarce imaginable to us in ''Europe''. The Propoſition and Demonſtration were fairly written on a thin Wafer, with Ink compoſed of a '''Cephalick''' Tincture. This the Student was to ſwallow upon a faſting Stomach, and for three days following eat nothing but Bread and Water. As the Wafer digeſted, the Tincture mounted to his Brain, bearing the Propoſition along with it.}}
## Of or relating to the [[cephalon]] (the head of a trilobite).
# {{lb|en|[[w:anatomical terms of location|anatomical terms of location and direction]]}} Toward the head; in bipeds such as humans, this direction corresponds to {{l|en|superior|id=anatomy}}.
#: {{syn|en|cephalad}}
#: {{ant|en|caudal}}
# [[headlike|Headlike]]; [[cephaloid#Adjective|cephaloid]].

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|medicine|obsolete}} A [[remedy]] that benefits the [[head]] or [[brain]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1707|author=Hans Sloane|title=A Voyage to the Islands Madera, Barbados, Nievas, S. Christophers and Jamaica|page=cliv
|passage={{...}} recover their Sight {{...}} by the use of Bleeding, Purging, Blistering and '''Cephalics'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1724|author=John Quincy|title=Pharmacopœia officinalis & extemporanea|page=595
|passage=All that of this Form could be titled ''Stomachics'', we have subjoin'd to this Division, because they are all of the ''Aromatic'' kind, and thereby claim equally to be '''''Cephalics'''''. The latter we have given, extend their Influences to the Head and whole nervous System, at the same time that they warm, comfort, and strengthen the Fibres of the Stomach, and dissipate Flatulencies, corrugate the Membranes, and promote Digestion: {{...}}}}
